issues.legal_issue: An insolvency resolution plan cannot authorize an encumbrance over public property owned by a third party when the legally required approval for dealing with that property has not been obtained.
material_facts: The municipal corporation owned the land on which the corporate debtor was developing a hospital; the land was not an asset owned by the corporate debtor.
The contract contemplated that the hospital project would be completed before a lease deed was executed, and permitted mortgages or charges only subject to the owner’s approval.
The project was not completed, and the municipal corporation had issued a show-cause notice proposing termination before insolvency proceedings began.
The resolution plan contemplated raising funds through a mortgage of the land, but the municipal corporation had not given the approval required to deal with its property.
The resolution plan was approved by the adjudicating authority despite the absence of that approval.
issues.conclusion: The resolution plan could not be approved insofar as it contemplated encumbering the municipal corporation’s land; it could be approved only to the extent that it did not affect that property. The insolvency appellate and adjudicating orders were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 92 and 92A of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act, 1888 prescribe how the corporation’s property may be dealt with, including the required approval. Section 238 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 gives the Code priority where there is an inconsistency, but does not override a third party’s control over its own property or remove a public body’s statutory duty to regulate that property. Where provisions can operate consistently, both should be given effect: Macquarie Bank Ltd. v. Shilpi Cable Technologies Ltd. (2018) 2 SCC 674. The Court also relied on the principle that a statutory power must be exercised in the prescribed manner or not at all, as expressed in Nazir Ahmad v. Emperor, AIR 1936 PC 253, Taylor v. Taylor, [1875] 1 Ch. D. 426, State of U.P. v. Singhara Singh, (1964) 4 SCR 485, Ram Singh Vijay Pal Singh v. State of U.P. (2007) 6 SCC 44, Essar Bulk Terminal Ltd. v. State of Gujarat (2018) 3 SCC 750, Saroj Screens Pvt. Ltd. v. Ghanshyam (2012) 11 SCC 434, and Dharani Sugars & Chemicals Ltd. v. Union of India (2019) 5 SCC 480. Jaipur Metals & Electricals Employees Organization v. Jaipur Metals & Electricals Ltd. (2019) 4 SCC 227 and Duncans Industries v. A.J. Agrochem, 2019 SCC OnLine SC 1319, were considered in addressing the effect of Section 238.

rule.if: insolvency_resolution_plan_approval and third_party_public_property_involved and plan_contemplates_encumbrance and required_owner_approval_absent

predicates.insolvency_resolution_plan_approval: The proceeding concerns approval of a plan to resolve a debtor’s insolvency.
predicates.third_party_public_property_involved: The property affected by the plan belongs to a public body rather than to the debtor.
predicates.plan_contemplates_encumbrance: The plan proposes to mortgage or otherwise encumber that property to support the debtor’s resolution.
predicates.required_owner_approval_absent: The approval required from the property-owning public body to deal with the property has not been obtained.
predicates.plan_cannot_authorize_encumbrance_of_thi: The plan cannot authorize an encumbrance of the public body’s property without the required approval.

issues.definition: When an insolvency plan proposes to encumber public property that belongs to someone other than the debtor, the plan cannot authorize that encumbrance if the required owner approval is absent.

issues.legal_issue: A contract providing for a lease after completion of a project does not itself vest a leasehold interest in the debtor when the project is not completed and no lease deed is executed.
material_facts: The contract provided that a lease deed would be executed after completion of the hospital project.
The corporate debtor did not complete the project within the stipulated period, and no lease deed was executed.
The contract also required payment of annual lease rentals, and the municipal corporation alleged defaults in those payments.
The municipal corporation issued a show-cause notice proposing termination before the insolvency process began; the Court did not determine whether the contract had in fact been terminated.
issues.conclusion: The contract remained an agreement to enter into a lease and did not itself confer a leasehold right or interest in the land. The Court did not decide whether the agreement had been terminated.
issues.legal_principle: On the terms of the contract, the lease was to be created by a later lease deed after project completion. Since the corporate debtor had not fulfilled the relevant conditions, the agreement did not itself vest a leasehold interest; a right to seek specific performance could arise if the obligations were fulfilled and the owner then failed to execute the lease. The Court left the disputed question of termination undecided.

rule.if: insolvency_resolution_plan_approval and lease_depends_on_project_completion and project_not_completed and lease_deed_not_executed

predicates.insolvency_resolution_plan_approval: The proceeding concerns approval of a plan to resolve a debtor’s insolvency.
predicates.lease_depends_on_project_completion: The parties’ agreement provides that a lease will be created only after completion of a project.
predicates.project_not_completed: The debtor did not complete the project required by the agreement.
predicates.lease_deed_not_executed: No lease deed was executed in favour of the debtor.
predicates.debtor_has_no_vested_leasehold_interest: The debtor has no leasehold interest vested in it under the uncompleted conditional lease arrangement.

issues.definition: If a debtor seeks insolvency-plan treatment of a lease that depends on project completion, but the project remains incomplete and no lease deed has been executed, the debtor has no vested leasehold interest.

issues.legal_issue: A public body is not bound by a representative’s acceptance of an insolvency plan when the required statutory approval has not been given and the representative’s authority to bind the body has not been established.
material_facts: The municipal corporation had made written submissions accepting the resolution plan or seeking its approval on stated terms.
The corporation had not approved the plan through the process required to authorize dealing with its property.
The record did not establish that the counsel or other representative who made the written submissions had authority to bind the corporation.
issues.conclusion: The written acceptance by counsel or another representative was inconclusive and did not bind the municipal corporation.
issues.legal_principle: There can be no estoppel against express provisions of law, and a representative’s statement cannot substitute for an approval required by law when that representative’s authority to bind the public body has not been established. The Court relied on Kasinka Trading v. Union of India (1995) 1 SCC 274, Darshan Oils (P) Ltd. v. Union of India (1995) 1 SCC 345, Shrijee Sales Corporation v. Union of India (1997) 3 SCC 398, Shree Sidhbali Steels Ltd. v. State of U.P. (2011) 3 SCC 193, Pappu Sweets and Biscuits v. Commissioner of Trade Tax, U.P. (1998) 7 SCC 228, and Commissioner of Customs v. Dilip Kumar & Co. (2018) 9 SCC 1.

predicates.insolvency_plan_approval_proceeding: The proceeding concerns approval of a plan to resolve a debtor’s insolvency.
predicates.public_body_property_requires_formal_app: The plan affects property of a public body for which the law requires formal approval.
predicates.formal_approval_absent: The public body has not given the approval required by law.
predicates.representative_concession_not_shown_auth: A representative has accepted the plan, but the representative’s authority to bind the public body has not been established.
predicates.public_body_not_bound_by_representative_: The public body is not bound by the representative’s concession in those circumstances.

issues.definition: A public body is not bound by a representative’s acceptance of an insolvency plan affecting its property when formal approval is required but absent and the representative’s authority to give binding acceptance has not been established.
